label.ja: 教育年数1年あたりの賃金上昇（世界平均）
label.en: Return to one extra year of schooling (global average)

effects.population: 1,120 estimates from 139 countries (mostly Mincerian earnings functions)

source.title: Returns to Investment in Education: A Decennial Review of the Global Literature
source.venue: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 8402

effects.quote: the private average global rate of return to one extra year of schooling is about 9 percent a year
effects.notes: Meta-summary of mostly OLS/Mincer estimates, so descriptive. No interval given in the abstract. The abstract also says returns are higher in low-income countries, so rich-country averages are typically somewhat lower; do not treat 9% as country-specific for the 7 target countries.

label.ja: 教育年数1年あたりの賃金上昇（日本・双子推定）
label.en: Return to one extra year of schooling (Japan, twins)

effects.population: Japanese twins, web-based survey

source.title: Estimating the Returns to Education Using a Sample of Twins - The case of Japan -
source.venue: RIETI Discussion Paper 12-E-076

effects.quote: although the conventional OLS estimate is 10.0%, we obtain 9.3% as the estimated rate of return to education
effects.notes: Within-twin estimate corrected for ability bias and measurement error. OLS counterpart in the same data is 10.0%. Confidence interval not in the abstract, so low/high are left null.

label.ja: 教育年数1年あたりの賃金上昇（米国・双子推定）
label.en: Return to one extra year of schooling (US, twins)

effects.population: Identical twins, Twinsburg (Ohio) Twins Festival survey, US, early 1990s

source.title: Estimates of the Economic Return to Schooling from a New Sample of Twins
source.venue: American Economic Review 84(5): 1157-1173 (NBER WP 4143)

effects.quote: Adjustment for measurement error indicates that an additional year of schooling increases wages by 16%
effects.notes: Measurement-error-corrected within-twin estimate from a small sample; widely regarded as on the high end of the literature. Old data (1991). Use as an upper-side reference, not a central estimate.

label.ja: 義務教育延長による1年の賃金効果（英国・男性）
label.en: Return to an extra compulsory school year (UK, men)

effects.population: British cohorts affected by the 1947 school-leaving-age reform (14 to 15); men, New Earnings Survey Panel Dataset

source.authors: Paul J. Devereux; Robert A. Hart
source.title: Forced to be Rich? Returns to Compulsory Schooling in Britain
source.venue: Economic Journal 120(549): 1345-1364

effects.quote: find similar estimates: zero returns for women and returns of 3 to 4% for men
effects.notes: Natural experiment (compulsory schooling law). The low/high here are the 3-4% range the abstract gives for men in the NESPD, not a confidence interval; with GHS data the abstract gives 4-7% for men. For women the abstract says zero. Re-analysis of Oreopoulos (2006), whose ~15% UK estimate was later corrected. Local effect for pupils who would otherwise leave at 14.

label.ja: 義務教育延長による1年の賃金効果（ドイツ）
label.en: Return to an extra compulsory school year (Germany)

effects.population: West German cohorts affected by state compulsory schooling reforms 1948-1970

source.title: Zero Returns to Compulsory Schooling in Germany: Evidence and Interpretation
source.venue: Review of Economics and Statistics 90(3): 592-598 (NBER WP 11414)

effects.quote: no return to compulsory schooling in Germany in terms of higher wages
effects.notes: Local effect of an extra year at the bottom of the distribution (extra 9th grade in Hauptschule), not a general return to schooling. Point 0 reflects the paper's headline 'zero return'; the exact standard error is not in the summary, so low/high are null. The authors suggest basic labour-market skills are learned earlier in Germany.

label.en: University vs high-school graduate wage ratio (Japan)

effects.population: General (mostly full-time) employees, both sexes, all ages, 2024; monthly scheduled cash earnings

source.authors: 厚生労働省 (Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Japan)
source.title: 令和6年賃金構造基本統計調査 結果の概況 (3) 学歴別にみた賃金 (2024 Basic Survey on Wage Structure, overview: wages by educational attainment)
source.venue: MHLW official statistics release

effects.quote: 男女計では、高校 288.9 千円、専門学校 306.9 千円、高専・短大 307.2 千円、大学 385.8 千円、大学院 497.0 千円
effects.notes: Computed as 385.8 / 288.9. Raw gap, not causal and not adjusted for age (average age 41.6 for university vs 46.2 for high school) or firm size. Within the age 40-44 band the ratio is similar (406.2 / 301.1 = 1.35). Japan is not in the OECD EAG relative-earnings dataset, so this national source is used instead. Scheduled earnings exclude bonuses and overtime.

label.ja: 英語力のある大卒者の所得差（日本）
label.en: Income gap for English-proficient university graduates (Japan)

effects.population: Japanese humanities/social-science university graduates, survey of about 13,000 (late 1990s)

source.title: The Economic Value of Foreign Language Proficiency in Labor Market (KAKEN project 10630040, final report summary)
source.venue: KAKEN (Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research) database; results reported in International Public Policy Studies 4(2)

effects.quote: Their income is higher than others by the degree of 20 to 30percent.
effects.notes: Earnings-function (OLS) estimate from a grant report summary, so descriptive and old (1998-99). Point 0.25 is the midpoint of the stated 20-30% range. Proficient workers were about 10% of the sample. A newer RIETI study (Sano, Tsuru, Kume, Yasui 2022, DP 22-E-080) finds a wage premium for English skill use but no uniform premium for English skill possession; its summary gives no number, so it is not included as a separate entry.

label.ja: 第二言語を話す大卒者の賃金プレミアム（米国）
label.en: Second-language wage premium for college graduates (US)

effects.population: Representative sample of US college graduates

source.title: Listening to What the World Says: Bilingualism and Earnings in the United States
source.venue: Review of Economics and Statistics 87(3): 523-538

effects.quote: suggest a 2%-3% wage premium for college graduates who can speak a second language
effects.notes: OLS with cognitive-ability controls, propensity-score and panel methods. Not a clean natural experiment, so labelled descriptive. Point is the midpoint of the stated range.

label.ja: 英仏バイリンガルの所得プレミアム（ケベック以外のカナダ・男性）
label.en: English-French bilingual earnings premium (Canada outside Quebec, men)

effects.population: Men outside Quebec, 2001 Census; compared with English-only speakers

source.title: The Economic Returns to the Knowledge and Use of a Second Official Language: English in Quebec and French in the Rest-of-Canada
source.venue: Canadian Public Policy 36(2): 137-158 (IZA DP 3551); figures from University of Guelph news release, 31 Aug 2010

effects.quote: bilingual men earn 3.6 per cent and bilingual women earn 6.6 per cent more than those who only speak English
effects.notes: Women: 6.6%. The paper's abstract (IZA DP 3551) calls the returns to using French at work outside Quebec 'much smaller, not statistically significant'. Caution: the Guelph release says 3.6% for men, but Globe and Mail and HR Reporter coverage say 3.8%; I could not check the paper's tables. Census cross-section, so descriptive.

label.ja: 英語もできる仏語話者男性の所得プレミアム（ケベック州）
label.en: Bilingual premium for francophone men who know English (Quebec)

effects.population: Francophone men in Quebec, 2001 Census; compared with French-only speakers

source.title: The Economic Returns to the Knowledge and Use of a Second Official Language: English in Quebec and French in the Rest-of-Canada
source.venue: Canadian Public Policy 36(2): 137-158 (IZA DP 3551); figures from University of Guelph news release, 31 Aug 2010

effects.quote: bilingual francophone men in Quebec earn up to seven per cent more than those who only speak French, and that number increases to almost 21 per cent for those who actually speak English on the job
effects.notes: About 21% for those who also use English at work. The paper's abstract reports 'very substantial, statistically significant, rewards to second official language use in Quebec'. Cross-sectional, so descriptive.

label.ja: 転職者と在職者の年間賃金上昇率の差（米国）
label.en: Job switchers vs stayers: gap in annual wage growth (US)

effects.population: US wage earners in the CPS observed 12 months apart; 12-month moving average of median hourly wage growth, Aug 2026

source.title: Wage Growth Tracker: 12-Month Moving Average of Unweighted Median Hourly Wage Growth, Job Switcher (FRBATLWGT12MMUMHWGJSW) and Job Stayer (FRBATLWGT12MMUMHWGJST)
source.venue: Atlanta Fed Wage Growth Tracker via FRED

effects.quote: 2026-08: job switcher 4.4; job stayer 3.6 (percent, 12-month moving average)
effects.notes: 0.008 = 4.4% - 3.6% nominal median wage growth, 12-month moving average, August 2026 (FRED data). The gap is cyclical: it was about 0.2 pp in Sep 2025 (4.3 vs 4.1) and much larger in 2022. Switchers include changes of occupation, industry or employer. Descriptive: switchers select into moves. The quote is a data record, not prose.

label.ja: 若年期の賃金上昇に占める転職時の上昇分（米国・男性）
label.en: Share of early-career wage growth from job changes (US, young men)

effects.population: Young US men, first 10 years in the labour market (LEED quarterly longitudinal data)

source.authors: Robert H. Topel; Michael P. Ward
source.title: Job Mobility and the Careers of Young Men
source.venue: Quarterly Journal of Economics 107(2): 441-479 (NBER WP 2649)

effects.quote: wage gains at job changes account for at least a third of early-career wage growth
effects.notes: This is a share of wage growth, not a per-move wage effect. It is a lower bound ('at least'), so high is null. The abstract says a typical young worker holds about seven employers in the first decade. Old data.

label.ja: 転職で賃金が増えた人の割合（日本）
label.en: Share of job changers whose wage rose (Japan)

effects.population: Job-changing hires in Japan, calendar year 2024 (Survey on Employment Trends)

source.authors: 厚生労働省 (Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Japan)
source.title: 令和6年雇用動向調査結果の概況 (2024 Survey on Employment Trends, overview)
source.venue: MHLW official statistics release

effects.quote: 前職の賃金と比べ「増加」した割合は40.5％、「減少」した割合は29.4％、「変わらない」の割合は28.4％
effects.notes: This is a distribution, not a wage effect: 40.5% saw a wage increase (29.4% by 10% or more), 29.4% a decrease (21.7% by 10% or more), 28.4% no change. Increases exceeded decreases by 16.3 pp among moves between permanent full-time workers. There is no mean or median wage change in this summary. Do not use it as a multiplicative premium.

label.ja: 職業免許の賃金プレミアム（米国）
label.en: Occupational licensing wage premium (US)

effects.population: US employees, specially designed national labour-force survey (Westat, 2008)

source.authors: Morris M. Kleiner; Alan B. Krueger
source.title: Analyzing the Extent and Influence of Occupational Licensing on the Labor Market
source.venue: Journal of Labor Economics 31(S1): S173-S202 (IZA DP 5505)

effects.quote: We find that licensing is associated with about 18 percent higher wages
effects.notes: Regression with controls, not causal. The earlier NBER WP 14979 version says 'about 14 percent'. The published version says the effect of government certification alone is 'much smaller'.

label.ja: 資格・免許保有者と非保有者の週給中央値の比（米国）
label.en: Median weekly earnings: with vs without certification/license (US)

effects.population: US full-time wage and salary workers aged 16+, 2025 annual averages (11 months, October missing)

source.title: Table 55. Median weekly earnings of full-time wage and salary workers by certification and licensing status and occupation, 2025 annual averages
source.venue: Current Population Survey, Labor Force Statistics

effects.notes: Computed as $1,460 (with a certification or license) / $1,131 (without). Raw gap, not adjusted for education, occupation or age. The license-only vs certification-only split was not used because my reads of the table's column order disagreed. No credible IT-certification estimate was found.

label.ja: 都市部と非都市部の賃金差（米国・横断面）
label.en: Urban vs non-urban wage gap (US, cross-section)

effects.population: US workers, metropolitan vs non-urban (1990s data)

source.authors: Edward L. Glaeser; David C. Maré
source.title: Cities and Skills
source.venue: Journal of Labor Economics 19(2): 316-342

effects.quote: Workers in cities earn 33% more than their nonurban counterparts.
effects.notes: Raw cross-sectional gap. The abstract says 'a portion of the urban wage premium is a wage growth, not a wage level, effect', so an immediate +33% on moving is not implied.

label.ja: 都市規模の賃金弾力性（短期・中期、スペイン）
label.en: Elasticity of earnings w.r.t. city size, short vs medium term (Spain)

effects.population: Spanish male employees, administrative social-security panel (MCVL), 2004-2009

source.authors: Jorge De la Roca; Diego Puga
source.title: Learning by Working in Big Cities
source.venue: Review of Economic Studies 84(1): 106-142

effects.quote: The estimated medium-term elasticity of 0.0510 is more than twice as large as the short-term elasticity of 0.0223
effects.notes: Worker fixed-effects panel. Point = medium-term elasticity (including learning); low = short-term static elasticity. About half the gain is static and half dynamic. The pooled-OLS elasticity is 0.0455 and falls to 0.0241 with worker fixed effects. Doubling city size raises earnings by about 2^0.051 - 1 = 3.6% in the medium term. Spanish data; tagged ALL as a transferable reference, not a target-country estimate.

label.ja: 大都市での1年目の経験による追加賃金（スペイン・マドリード/バルセロナ）
label.en: Extra earnings from first year of experience in the biggest cities (Spain)

effects.population: Spanish male employees; Madrid/Barcelona vs cities outside the top five

source.authors: Jorge De la Roca; Diego Puga
source.title: Learning by Working in Big Cities
source.venue: Review of Economic Studies 84(1): 106-142

effects.quote: A first year of experience raises earnings an additional 3.1% if this was acquired in the two biggest cities instead of outside the top five
effects.notes: Worker fixed-effects estimate. The paper says this experience premium stays with workers after they leave. For comparison, workers in Madrid earn 18% more than observationally similar workers in Utrera (the smallest city) before fixed effects. The premium per year decays with overall experience.

label.ja: 東京都と全国平均の賃金比（日本・横断面）
label.en: Tokyo vs national average wage ratio (Japan, cross-section)

effects.population: General (mostly full-time) employees, both sexes, 2024; monthly scheduled cash earnings

source.authors: 厚生労働省 (Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, Japan)
source.title: 令和6年賃金構造基本統計調査 結果の概況 (11) 都道府県別にみた賃金
source.venue: MHLW official statistics release

effects.quote: 全国計（ 330.4 千円）よりも賃金が高かったのは ４都府県（東 京都、神奈川県、愛知県、大阪府）となっており、最も高かったのは、東京都（ 403.7 千円）
effects.notes: Computed as 403.7 / 330.4. Raw gap that reflects Tokyo's mix of industries, firm sizes and education. It does not account for Tokyo's higher cost of living. Per De la Roca and Puga (2017) and Glaeser and Maré (2001), only part of such gaps is an immediate effect of moving.
